summary: Master petroleum economics and finance through our specialized course. Gain essential skills in operations cost auditing to optimize your business strategies.
lede: Petroleum project economics and operations cost auditing assess project value, fiscal terms, and whether operating costs are properly allocated and supported. For professionals involved in asset valuation, capital planning, finance, or cost control, the course develops practical skills in Excel-based cash-flow and scenario modeling, production-sharing contract analysis, joint-venture cost allocation, and risk-based audit planning.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already contribute to petroleum asset valuation, capital planning, or cost control and need a more rigorous, audit-ready approach.
modules: Measurement, Metrics, and Petroleum Fiscal Systems
Joint Venture Economics and Cost Allocation
Operations Cost Auditing in Oil and Gas
Unit Costs, Variance Analysis, and Benchmarks
prerequisites: This 5-day intermediate-to-advanced course assumes you already work with financial data, budgets, or economic evaluations in the energy sector or a related capital-intensive industry. You should be comfortable with core finance concepts such as time value of money, NPV/IRR, and basic financial statements, and be able to use Excel for formulas, charts, and simple data tables. Prior exposure to oil and gas operations, reserves, or joint ventures is highly beneficial but not mandatory, as the course builds petroleum-specific context before deepening into economics and operations cost auditing. You will need a laptop with a current version of Microsoft Excel and the ability to work with provided datasets and templates.
